item.title: Modeling Longitudinal Data Using Matrix Completion
item.description:
We use matrix completion to estimate smooth individual trajectories from sparse and irregular longitudinal measurements. The framework also supports multivariate measurements and regression.

Published in Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics, 33(2), 551–566 (2024), following online publication on November 15, 2023. Read the published paper.

Earlier versions circulated as Longitudinal data analysis using matrix completion. The preprint and fcomplete package remain available.

item.title: OpenCap: Human movement dynamics from smartphone videos
item.description:
OpenCap combines video-based pose estimation, machine learning, and biomechanical simulation to estimate human movement and musculoskeletal forces from two or more smartphone cameras.

Scott D. Uhlrich, Antoine Falisse, and Lukas Kidzinski contributed equally to this work.

Read the published paper for the methods, validation, and study limitations.

item.title: Wearable sensors enable personalized predictions of clinical laboratory measurements
item.description:
We studied how physiological data from consumer wearable devices can be used with machine learning to predict clinical laboratory measurements and support longitudinal health monitoring.

Jessilyn Dunn and Lukas Kidzinski contributed equally to this work.

Published in Nature Medicine, 27, 1105–1112 (2021). Read the published paper for the methods, findings, and limitations. An author manuscript is available through PubMed Central.

item.title: Deep neural networks enable quantitative movement analysis using single-camera videos
item.description:
We developed machine learning methods for estimating gait metrics from ordinary single-camera videos of children with cerebral palsy. The work explores how computer vision could make quantitative movement analysis more accessible.

Lukas Kidzinski and Bryan Yang contributed equally to this work.

Read the published paper for the methods, validation, and study limitations.
